evidence: Hydatius, Chronicon: ad Brācaram extrēmam cīvitātem Gallaeciae
Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Braga: Bracara Augusta
terms.comment: Pliny names it the town of the Brācarī called Augusta (NH 4.112); the short Brācara is in Hydatius’s fifth-century chronicle. The long ā is that of the people’s name, Brācarī (Lewis & Short, citing the same passage of Pliny). A town takes no preposition: Brācaram Augustam (to), Brācarae Augustae (in, at), Brācarā Augustā (from).

sources: J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
The Latin Library texts (thelatinlibrary.com), read in a local copy, for ancient passages not quoted in Lewis & Short; cited by book and section.
